title: Distinct Subsequences
pattern: 2-D DP: use the letter or skip it
statement: Given strings `s` and `t`, return the number of distinct **subsequences of `s`** that are equal to `t` — the number of ways to delete letters from `s` so that `t` remains.
picture: Picture a grid of boxes: *in how many ways can the first `j` letters of `t` be picked out of the first `i` letters of `s`?* An empty `t` can always be picked out in exactly one way: pick nothing. For any other box, look at the newest letter of `s`. You can always skip it, keeping the count from the box above. If it matches the newest letter of `t`, you can also use it, adding the count from the box diagonally up-left.
idea: Let `dp[i][j]` be the number of ways to form the first `j` letters of `t` from the first `i` letters of `s`.

Look at the last letter of that prefix of `s`. It can always be **skipped**: `dp[i − 1][j]` ways. If it equals the last needed letter of `t`, it can also be **used** for it: then the earlier letters must form the rest, `dp[i − 1][j − 1]` ways.
An empty `t` can be formed in exactly one way from any prefix (delete everything), so the first column is 1.

say.1: LeetCode puts every answer inside a class named `Solution`. It is only a wrapper: the real work happens in the function below it.
say.2: The function we must write. It gets `s` and `t`, and returns in how many ways `t` can be picked out of `s`, keeping the order.
say.6: A grid of boxes: `dp[i][j]` is the number of ways to pick the first `j` letters of `t` out of the first `i` letters of `s`.
say.10: Picking out an empty `t` works in exactly one way: pick nothing.
say.12: Fill in the other boxes, row by row: one more letter of `s` in each row.
say.13: And across each row: one more letter of `t` in each column.
say.14: Does the newest letter of `s` match the newest letter of `t`?
say.16: Then either use it (the ways in the box diagonally up-left) or skip it (the ways in the box above). Add both.
say.19: Otherwise it cannot be used here: skip it, keeping the count from the box above.
say.21: The bottom-right box: the ways to pick all of `t` out of all of `s`.
